name: Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor
positioning: French Art Deco hotel opened in 1932 in Siem Reap's Old French Quarter, with a personal butler for every stay
best_for: Travelers using Siem Reap as a base for the temples of Angkor
Guests interested in hotel history and Khmer cuisine

facts.text: The hotel was built in French Art Deco style with local influences.
In 2019 the hotel underwent an extensive renovation that restored its rooms, suites and architectural features.
The hotel is in the Old French Quarter of Siem Reap, facing the Royal Palace and close to the Angkor National Museum.
The new Siem Reap International Airport is 48 km from the hotel.
Every stay is accompanied by a personal butler.
Herbs and spices for Restaurant 1932 are gathered daily in the hotel gardens.
Afternoon Tea is served in the conservatory with a resident pianist.
The hotel describes Elephant Bar cocktail hour as a Siem Reap institution.
Raffles Spa offers authentic Khmer massages alongside modern treatments.
The hotel has two professional tennis courts with a resident coach.

highlights.text: The original timber elevator in the lobby is described as the oldest lift in Indochina.
Following a Royal Guard tradition, the doormen wear silk pantaloons whose colour changes with the day of the week.
Restaurant 1932 offers four tasting menus conceived by Siem Reap native Chef Dorn Doeurt with Executive Chef Memo Hernandez.
The swimming pool was modelled after the ancient baths of Angkor.
The hotel's events space hosts traditional Khmer dance performances every Saturday night.

considerations.text: The hotel is in town rather than at the temples; the temples of Angkor are an 8 km ride away.
The hotel names November to February as the ideal time to visit, when the weather is cooler.
Restaurant 1932 has a dress code; slip-ons and flip-flops are not permitted.
